== Biography ==
('''research-in-progress''': James Glasgow Missouri death certificate n.d. pre-1910, death at 72 years old in St. Louis County, says he is from Christiana (a town in Pennsylvania), so this could be him. http://www.sos.mo.gov/archives/resources/birthdeath/deaths.asp?BirthId=124173)

Iniitally we had "James H Glasgow" whereas the later GEDCOM download says "James Albert Glasco". Presumed the "A" was poorly written and looked like an H so went with the full middle name of "Albert."

== Research Notes ==
=== Source and next-question reconciliation —24October2026 ===

The earlier compatible-only question about Chester estate7520’s testator has been superseded by the24October Samuel-2872 identity review: the combined memorial family names Judith,Tabitha and Margaret Ellen identify that testator at98%. This does not name the Missouri James as a son. Samuel’s own preferred father James-1025 is a separate67% inference, not evidence of James-45’s parentage. James’s father remains unknown and no percentage is assigned. Read Samuel’s current account before repeating its identity test. The next unperformed candidate test is the1825 Huntingdon will of John-1549; compare any named James and his residence/family with the drummer and Missouri household. The York Bible and immigrant-father tradition remain separate tests.<ref>Chester County Register of Wills, estate7520, Samuel Glasgow of West Fallowfield, [https://portal.laserfiche.com/Portal/DocView.aspx?id=773006&page=588&repo=r-24f48cc6 original will, portal pp.588–589],17May1824, proved31May1824; original reading23October2026 reused. Compared in the existing24October review with [https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/75056130/samuel_glasgow memorial75056130], its Judith,Tabitha and Margaret Ellen family links and specified stone photograph; contributor links are not original vital proof. No new source inspection in this reconciliation.</ref>

Earlier dated discussions below retain their original wording; the source-target and completed-test statements above supersede those particular questions.

=== Downington army record — 23 October 2026 ===

The original army register gives James Glasgow/Glassgow, aged 21, a '''drummer''', born '''“Downington,” Pennsylvania''', enlisted29 December 1818 at '''Philadelphia'''. Entry404 is in 5th Infantry, Co. G; it gives stature 5 ft 5 in and service remarks continuing through30 June 1821. [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=USM%2FENLIST%2F11887224271 Findmypast transcript] and [https://search.findmypast.co.uk/record?id=USM%2FENLIST%2F005257035%2F00272&parentid=USM%2FENLIST%2F11887224271 original image]; NARA M233,roll 15,volume 029,p. 37; Findmypast image 005257035/00272. Original entry and column headings inspected 23 October 2026. The licensed scan is retained privately. The already cited [https://familysearch.org/pal:/MM9.1.1/QJD5-P8NN FamilySearch record] refers to the same entry, not an independent record.

This is a '''probable record match''' to James-45: his c1796 Pennsylvania birth and later drummer history fit the 1818 enlistee. The register does not name a Missouri residence, wife or parent. [http://drw.50webs.com/will.html Dan Williams’s descendant narrative], sections “The Missouri Years” and “James Glasco,” describes the later James’s 1846 drummer service, a Philadelphia birth and an immigrant father’s estate. Its[http://drw.50webs.com/Williams/wcredits.html credits],notes 10/13, identify family recollection and say the father’s country is undetermined. That narrative’s5 ft 4 in differs from this entry’s5 ft 5 in. These differences remain visible; the register’s age does not establish an exact birth date.

'''Next family test:''' Downington is compatible with modern Downingtown in Chester County; this is the specific locality to test before another Pennsylvania-wide search. [[Glasgow-2872|Samuel Glasgow-2872]],1761 Nottingham–1824 Cochranville, is a local generation-compatible candidate, but has no held Downingtown address or James-son clause and his Pennsylvania birth conflicts with a literal immigrant-father tradition. [[Glasgow-1549|John Glasgow-1549]],the Scottish-born Sinking Valley man, remains a compatible immigrant alternative; his 1825 Huntingdon will is not read. [[Glasgow-2873|Hugh Glasgow-2873]] is another compatible generation with a distinct existing James Ramsay son. [[Glasgow-2871|John-2871]] and [[Glasgow-2870|John-2870]] died before the enlistee’s estimated birth and cannot be his father on these dates. No named father or mother is selected; an unselected locality lead is not a new genealogical join. Inspect a Chester probate/heir instrument and the cited York Glasgow Family Bible, then compare the Philadelphia-estate tradition.

The existing Pennsylvania birth field and all family links are preserved while the enlistee’s later identity is tested. The separate Christiana/StLouis death-index candidate remains unverified; it is not made the Missouri man’s identity by this army entry.

=== Place and estate locator ===

The register’s Downington is geographically compatible with modern Downingtown, Chester County; this does not prove the Missouri identity. [https://www.downingtown.org/254/History Borough history] describes the local name after the War of 1812.

The [https://www.chesco.org/DocumentCenter/View/83366/Wills-and-Administrations-1714-1923 official Chester County index], PDF p. 420, lists Samuel Glasgow, 1824, file 7520, West Fallowfield, with will, inventory and accounts. The index does not name James or prove this is Samuel-2872’s estate. The original was subsequently read through the official portal. The testator names wife Tabitha, infant daughter Margaret Ellen and brothers William, James and Robert Glasgow of Ireland; no Missouri James is named as a son. The testator’s identity with [[Glasgow-2872]] remains unproved. [https://portal.laserfiche.com/Portal/DocView.aspx?id=773006&page=588&repo=r-24f48cc6 Original will, portal pp. 588–589]. No father is selected.

== Biography ==
Current Research-in-progress: I stumbled across someone on the internet that was able to verify through family history and stories what I'd suspected of James Glasgow being a drummer.  The biographical write-up is fabulous: http://drw.50webs.com/will.html  I think perhaps I have found James' father's name, but I haven't found any more supporting evidence.  Since Philadelphia's records are still getting added to the internet, this may take me a while if I'm able to find confirmation at all.  [[Woodland-151|Woodland-151]]

James married Elizabeth Groff on June 12th, 1825 in Franklin County, Missouri.
